A spiritual sequel to Left 4 Dead, with modern features like a progression system, iron sights, and better graphics. I don't get the hate for this game; I find it very enjoyable.

Some players are complaining that the game is "abandoned". That's not accurate; it's FINISHED. It's a complete game with plenty of content, and replay value. The DLC adds even more great new content and replay value to what is already a solid base game.
it's really fun with friends not so much with randos that try to solo everything

[h1]Not The ROI I Was Banking On - Turtle Rock Exec[/h1]

Ah, Back 4 Blood! The highly-anticipated spiritual successor to that other game where you team up with friends to smack down some very rude undead party crashers. I was told this game was a surefire hit. As a discerning (and dare I say, shrewd) individual with a vested interest in profitable ventures, I had high hopes!

From the trailers, one can see the compelling gunplay, the frenzied hordes of zombies, and the dynamic team cooperation. But where, oh where, is the money machine I was promised? I was assured that every bullet, every medkit, and every ounce of survivor's sweat could be turned into a shiny gold coin. Alas, it seems my dreams of swimming in a pool of digital earnings á la Scrooge McDuck might be slightly... postponed.

As I scrutinized the game (from my shareholder's perspective, of course), I couldn’t help but notice that despite the tantalizing microtransactions and hypermonetization avenues, the piles of gold weren't exactly stacking up to the ceiling of my penthouse. Perhaps the player base is too busy enjoying the game? Or maybe they're just stashing their pennies away in a big clay jar like my bubbe used to do.

Truth be told, I haven’t actually played the game (who has the time between stock market dives and perusing diamond catalogs?), but I did attend a very informative shareholder meeting (bagels and lox included) where they assured me this game was going to be bigger than sliced challah bread.

In conclusion, if you’re looking for a frenetic co-op shooter that harkens back to the golden age of zombie mayhem, Back 4 Blood might just be your jam. And if you happen to have any business tips on how to... encourage further profitability, do drop me a line. Preferably written on a $100 bill.
